title: "Open points"

This page lists what is not done, not known or not decided. Each item keeps the default
of the package until the author decides.

## Comparisons against published values

A benchmarks page with comparisons against published values comes later. This work is
not started.

## The G-ADOPT comparison

The comparison with the geoid of G-ADOPT waits for one answer. It is not yet known what
the G-ADOPT geoid includes: self-gravitation, the deflected boundaries, and the pressure
density under the anelastic liquid approximation. The flags of `stokesjx` can then reproduce the same
problem.

## Physics not implemented

- **The anelastic liquid approximation (ALA).** ALA adds entries to the radial momentum
  row of the matrix A. It needs a compressibility profile and a Poisson source.
- **Partial slip.** A partial-slip boundary is a new boundary class with a traced
  parameter. The interface is in the docstring of `BoundaryCondition`. Its degree-1 frame
  rule is open: the class carries a tangential traction, and the frame rule then treats
  it as an anchored boundary.

## TALA and movable boundaries

Under TALA two properties of the discrete model remain ([derivatives](gradients.qmd#the-limits-under-tala)):

- the kernels jump when a viscosity cut crosses a density pair: 0.5 to 2.5 % of the
  geoid field at viscosity contrasts 3 to 100, and 1.0 to 1.5 nat per crossing of an HMC
  trajectory at $\sigma_r = 10$ km for 1e22 | 1e21 Pa s;
- the cut has small kinks at the input nodes: $E_{rms}$ 0.036 nat at a viscosity contrast
  of 10 and 0.061 nat at 1.1 on a range that ends at the density pair.

## Small known limits

- The bound of the comparison with the mpmath reference has a small margin in the raw
  frame at `l = 1`: 4.6e-13 against 1e-12.
- `Layers.pairs` and `MovableRange.members` hold the value `-1` for a cut boundary. `-1`
  is a valid NumPy index, so a caller must test for it before an index operation.
- `Layers.sheet_mass(density, kernels)` takes its arguments in the opposite order to
  `Layers.fields(kernels, density)`.

## Release

The version is `0.0.1.dev0`. There is no release, no `CITATION.cff` and no PyPI package
yet.

## Outside this package

The joint inversion with lovejx is later work outside this package. `stokesjx` supplies
the values and the derivatives for it.
